provisional: the list of bootloader pins is from memory of ST AN2606 (not readable here; a web-search extract of a third-party copy agrees for USART1-3, I2C1-3, SPI1, FDCAN1); only the existence of each peripheral function on its pin is verified below
OVM7692 pins are assumed to have ordinary protection diodes to their (unpowered) supply: a line that ends only on unpowered camera pins then sits below a diode drop

which pulls the ROM enables is not known (AN2606 as remembered: pull-down on the SPI pins, pull-up on the USART pins, none on the I2C pins). The verdicts above hold for that set and for no pulls at all. A 40 kohm pull AGAINST a 100 kohm board resistor could only come from a pull-down on a USART receive pin (PA3, PA10: a break condition on a UART nobody uses) or a pull-up on I2C2_SCL (PB10: the LCD is selected and receives no clock); neither loads an output
SPI protocol of the ROM (sync byte 0x5A on MOSI clocked by SCK): memory of ST AN4286

what the UCPD pads do is from memory of ST RM0456 / DS13086 (not read): after reset a HIGH level on a DBCC pad switches a 5.1 kohm pull-down onto its CC pad until firmware sets UCPD_DBDIS; the CC pads are ST's FT_c structure, whose output drive is not known here. WHICH pads these are is read from the pin data
electrical limits of the pins (thresholds, 8 mA / 20 mA, PC13 limited to 3 mA sink, injection current) are from memory of DS13086, not read

ucpd_pad_reasons.CHG_STAT: an INPUT (open-drain CHG of the charger, 100 kohm to V2V8): nothing depends on the pad's output stage; a dead-battery pull-down before UCPD_DBDIS is set only makes it read 'charging' (27 uA through the pull-up) while nobody reads it
ucpd_pad_reasons.SPI2_MOSI: an alternate-function output into one CMOS input of the IMU (microamperes); a dead-battery pull-down while PB14 is high costs 2.8 V / 5.1 kohm = 0.55 mA only while the line is driven high, and holds the floating line low in reset
ucpd_pad_reasons.SPI1_MOSI: dead-battery control pad of PA15: it floats in reset and in the ROM bootloader (no board pull, by the spec), so the pull-down on PA15 may or may not be there - PA15 carries an input for that reason
ucpd_pad_reasons.SPI2_MISO: dead-battery control pad of PB15: the IMU's SDO, high-impedance while the IMU is not selected; firmware keeps an internal pull-down on it between transfers

firmware_notes: Regenerate gl_pins.h from pinmap.json (every row marked CHANGED moved).

CHG_INHIBIT (PH1) is a PUSH-PULL output, HIGH = stop charging (it turns on Q1, which pulls the charger's TS input low); analog or low = charger on. The present firmware (drivers/power.c, inhibit_(): latch low, then open drain) does NOTHING on this board - the gate of Q1 never goes high - so the firmware's own 0 to 45 C charge gate is inoperative until inhibit_() drives the pin push-pull HIGH. Until then only the charger's hardware TS window acts.

CHG_STAT is on PA15 (EXTI15): the BQ25101's open-drain CHG output with a 100 kohm pull-up to V2V8, low = charging, high = not charging, done or no VBUS. No internal pull is needed. With the BQ25100 fallback fitted every internal pull on PA15 must be off (it also has the JTDI pull-up until the firmware switches to SWD only).

EXTI lines: IMU_INT1 PA7 = EXTI7 (WKUP8), IMU_INT2 PA5 = EXTI5, VBUS_SENSE PC13 = EXTI13 (WKUP2), CHG_STAT PA15 = EXTI15. hal/stm32u5/gl_hal_stm32u5.c hard-codes EXTI13 / 5 / 9 / 0 (vectors and compile-time asserts): three of the four must move.

UCPD (PROVISIONAL, RM0456 / DS13086 not read): PA15 and PB15 are the UCPD1 CC pads, PB5 and PB14 their dead-battery control pads. After reset a high level on PB5 (SPI1_MOSI) switches a 5.1 kohm pull-down onto PA15, a high level on PB14 (SPI2_MISO) one onto PB15 (SPI2_MOSI: 0.55 mA while it is driven high). Set UCPD_DBDIS in PWR_UCPDR (HAL_PWREx_DisableUCPDDeadBattery) at the top of gl_hal_init(), before any pin is configured, and again after every wake-up that resets the PWR registers.
PA9 is USB_OTG_FS_VBUS and carries GRAIN_CP0: run the USB device with VBUS sensing off and tell the core that the session is valid from VBUS_SENSE (register details PROVISIONAL).

USB supply: set the USB-supply-valid bit only while BOTH VBUS_SENSE (PC13) is high AND the MCU's own VDDUSB monitor reports the supply ready; clear it on the falling edge of either. PC13 alone does not measure VDDUSB: on undocking VDDUSB can fall below 3.0 V within about a millisecond under USB load while PC13 still reads high for up to about 22 ms.
VBUS_SENSE: divider 100 kohm : 100 kohm on the VBUS pad (not behind the Schottky). High is guaranteed above 3.92 V at the pad, low below 1.68 V; removal from the cradle is seen within about 22 ms.
CAM_R_PWDN is on PH3, the BOOT0 pad (10 kohm to ground): it reads low at every reset; 0.28 mA flows into the pull-down while it is driven high.
IMU_CS is PB1 and LCD_DISP is PB12 (exchanged: PB12 is the ROM bootloader's SPI2 chip-select input).
Before a jump to the ROM bootloader leave the IMU with its INT2 output static (data-ready routing off): PA5 / PA7 are the ROM's SPI1 clock and data inputs.

The grain bias divider hangs on LCD_DISP (PB12): DISP must have been high for 35 ms before a grain measurement. drivers/grain_frontend.c waits 25 ms after it enables the op-amp and does not look at the display: gl_grain_fe_power() must wait for, or refuse without, 35 ms of display-on time.
Switch PA15, PB3, PB4 away from JTAG (SWD only).
Every camera-facing pin low or analog while V2V8_CAM is off: PC0, PC1, PC3 (SCCB), PC2, PH3 (PWDN), the eleven DCMI pins and PA8.

Lines without a board pull float while the MCU is in reset or in the ROM bootloader: LCD_EXTCOMIN (PB2), SPI1_SCK / SPI1_MOSI (PB3 / PB5), SPI2_SCK / SPI2_MOSI (PB13 / PB15), CAM_L_PWDN (PC2). gl_hal_init() must give each its level before anything else; keep an internal pull-down on PB4 and PB14 (the MISO lines float between transfers; PB14 is also UCPD1_DBCC2).
PA3 (OPAMP1 output, the ROM's USART2_RX) is held high by R31, 150 kohm to V2V8, also with light on the photodiode. Leave PA3 analog while OPAMP1 is off: driven low it costs 19 uA.
